anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the INA219 (U1) has SCL (pin 5) and SDA (pin 6) labeled I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC, with address pins A0 (7) and A1 (8) tied to GND, and the sheet note reads 'I2C address: 0x40'. On the FCC Peripherals sheet the PCA9685 (U2) has SCL (pin 26) and SDA (pin 27) on the same I2C2_SCL_FCC / I2C2_SDA_FCC nets, with all six address pins A0–A5 (pins 1–5 and 24) tied to GND, giving the same 0x40 address (its note also reads 'I2C address: 0x40'). Two different devices with identical 7-bit addresses therefore sit on one shared bus.
anomalies.expected: The specification lists both devices as populated, functioning parts: 'TI INA219AIDCNR, I2C addr 0x40' and 'NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40'. Two devices that must both be addressable cannot share one I2C bus at the same address; either one device belongs on a different bus (e.g. I2C3_FCC, which the FCC sheet shows wired only to an external connector) or one device's address straps must differ so the addresses are unique. The spec's known-issues section documents only the barometer pin swap, not an I2C address collision, so the intended design cannot have contained this.

evidence.quote: Power sheet: U1 INA219AIDCNR pin 5 -> I2C2_SCL_FCC, pin 6 -> I2C2_SDA_FCC, pins 7/8 (A0/A1) -> GND, note 'I2C address: 0x40'
FCC Peripherals sheet: U2 PCA9685PW pin 26 -> I2C2_SCL_FCC, pin 27 -> I2C2_SDA_FCC, pins 1-5 and 24 (A0-A5) -> GND, note 'I2C address: 0x40'
Current/voltage sensor ... TI INA219AIDCNR, I2C addr 0x40 ... PWM/servo driver ... NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: I2C bus contention on I2C2_FCC: the FCC cannot address the PCA9685 servo driver and the INA219 power monitor independently (both ACK 0x40), corrupting PWM/servo output and battery voltage/current sensing, or hanging the bus entirely.

parsed.summary: Most of the drawing matches the specification (rail values, R1 = 10 mOhm, L1 = 15 uH, Vout = 0.8*(1+R5/R6) with 6k8/1k3, the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap, CH330 bridges, crystal parts, etc.), but the PCA9685 and the INA219 are both strapped to I2C address 0x40 and wired to the same I2C2_FCC bus, which contradicts the spec's intent that both devices be addressable and constitutes a real functional anomaly.
